subject: Computer Networking
title: Wi-Fi Offloading
description: A micro-lesson that makes Wi-Fi Offloading usable.

hook.text: Your phone switches to Wi-Fi at home, saving your mobile data. Carriers encourage this — it saves them bandwidth too.

buildup.text: Wi-Fi offloading moves traffic from the cellular network to local Wi-Fi. Both the user and carrier benefit.

discovery.text: Passpoint lets your phone automatically join trusted Wi-Fi networks without you typing a password.

twist.text: Over half of all mobile data is actually carried by Wi-Fi. The cellular network couldn't handle it all alone.

climax.text: 5G small cells and Wi-Fi 6 are converging. Future networks may blend both seamlessly without users noticing.

punchline.text: Wi-Fi offloading keeps cellular networks from collapsing.

quiz.question: Why do carriers encourage Wi-Fi offloading?
options: It reduces load on their cellular network
Wi-Fi is always faster than cellular
It allows them to charge more for data

details.summary: Wi-Fi offloading shifts mobile data traffic from cellular networks to Wi-Fi when available, reducing congestion on cellular towers and saving data costs.
details.whyItMatters: The majority of smartphone data traffic is already offloaded to Wi-Fi. Offloading is a critical strategy for mobile operators managing limited cellular spectrum capacity.
takeaways: Over half of mobile data traffic is offloaded to Wi-Fi networks
Passpoint enables automatic secure connections to carrier hotspots
Offloading reduces cellular congestion during peak usage times

faq.question: What is Passpoint and how does it work?
faq.answer: Passpoint, based on the Hotspot 2.0 standard, allows devices to discover and connect to Wi-Fi networks automatically using credentials stored on the SIM card or from the mobile operator.

faq.question: Why do carriers invest in Wi-Fi offloading?
faq.answer: Licensed cellular spectrum is expensive and limited. When users connect to Wi-Fi, their traffic no longer consumes cellular capacity. This lets carriers serve more customers without buying additional spectrum.
